kinds.vendor-hosted: Run by the vendor. You connect to a remote endpoint.
kinds.vendor-local: Published by the vendor. You run it on your machine, usually for developers.
kinds.vendor-open-source: Open source from the vendor. You run it yourself.
kinds.community: Built and maintained by someone other than the vendor.
kinds.integration-layer: Works across many connected apps, not one.

servers.name: Hosted MCP servers
servers.covers: Expose capabilities of a Salesforce org to outside AI clients.
servers.auth: An external client app for authentication.
servers.notes: Sources disagree on whether these are beta or generally available. Check Salesforce's current documentation.

servers.name: Salesforce DX MCP server
servers.covers: Developer tooling: development, testing and deployment from an agentic IDE.
servers.notes: For developers, not for business users working with records. Some sources describe it as beta.

servers.name: Remote MCP server
servers.covers: Read and write access to CRM data such as contacts and deals.
servers.notes: Aimed at MCP-compatible AI tools and agents.

servers.name: Developer MCP server
servers.covers: Helps coding agents work with the HubSpot developer platform, such as scaffolding and deploying apps and CMS assets.
servers.notes: Not a CRM data server. It is a developer tool.

servers.name: Dataverse MCP server (Dynamics 365 CRM data)
servers.covers: MCP access to Dataverse, the data platform under Dynamics 365 CRM apps.
servers.notes: Confirm scope and status on Microsoft Learn. Details came from secondary sources.

servers.name: Dynamics 365 Customer Service MCP server
servers.covers: Customer service data in Dynamics 365.
servers.notes: Reported as generally available in 2026, while a Microsoft connector page still labeled it preview. Check current status.

servers.name: AI Connector Service and MCP Standard Tools SuiteApp
servers.covers: An MCP layer inside NetSuite. The MCP Standard Tools SuiteApp supplies default tools such as record access, saved searches, reports and metadata lookups, and you can build your own tools.
servers.notes: Guides report that the Administrator role cannot be used. The AI client may need its own paid plan. Verify setup in Oracle's current help.

servers.name: Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server (Finance and Operations)
servers.covers: MCP access to Dynamics 365 ERP data.
servers.notes: Was a preview, enabled through Feature management, as of late 2025. Check current status.

servers.name: SAP BTP administration MCP server
servers.covers: Administering SAP BTP accounts.
servers.auth: Requires access to a BTP global account.
servers.notes: Listed as official by a directory. Access to business data in S/4HANA is mostly community-built on OData and BAPI. Verify in SAP's help portal.

servers.name: QuickBooks Online MCP server
servers.covers: The QuickBooks Online API: create, read, update, delete and search across entities, and financial reports.
servers.notes: A hosted option exists in some AI clients. Availability varies by region and client.

servers.name: Community servers and modules
servers.covers: Access to Odoo data from AI clients.
servers.notes: No vendor-official server was found. Some options are modules installed on your Odoo server, and some are paid third-party modules.

servers.name: Community servers
servers.covers: Invoices, contacts, expenses, inventory and sales orders in several community projects.
servers.notes: No official Zoho server was confirmed when checked.

servers.name: Supabase MCP server
servers.covers: The Supabase platform: database, auth and edge functions.
servers.notes: Documents a read-only mode.

servers.name: Neon MCP server
servers.covers: Managing Neon Postgres projects and branches, running SQL and migrations.
servers.notes: Write mode can create projects and branches, which can add cost.

servers.name: MongoDB MCP Server and Atlas managed MCP
servers.covers: Atlas, Atlas Local, Community and Enterprise deployments. A managed, hosted option runs in Atlas.
servers.auth: Database credentials or Atlas API access.
servers.notes: A read-only configuration is available.

servers.name: Snowflake managed MCP server
servers.covers: Cortex Agents, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search and SQL execution.
servers.auth: Governed by Snowflake role-based access control.
servers.notes: Access follows the roles you grant.

servers.name: Managed MCP servers
servers.covers: Unity Catalog functions, Genie, vector search and, on some clouds, SQL.
servers.auth: Unity Catalog permissions apply to every server.
servers.notes: Documented as preview when checked. The server set differs by cloud.

servers.name: MCP Toolbox for Databases
servers.covers: Prebuilt tools for BigQuery, AlloyDB, Cloud SQL, Spanner, Firestore, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MongoDB, or custom tools defined in YAML.
servers.notes: Sources differ on how it is classified. Treat it as Google's open-source project.

servers.name: ClickHouse MCP server
servers.covers: Querying ClickHouse. ClickHouse Cloud also offers a managed remote server with more tools, including management operations.
servers.auth: OAuth on the managed remote server.
servers.notes: A different community server also exists. Check which one you are installing.

servers.name: Redis MCP server
servers.covers: A natural-language interface to manage and search data in Redis.
servers.notes: A separate Redis Cloud API server handles administration only and does not read or write data.

servers.name: Community servers
servers.covers: Inspecting and querying MySQL databases.
servers.notes: No Oracle-published server was found. Use a read-only database user.

servers.name: Community and provider-hosted servers
servers.covers: Querying Postgres. Several community servers exist, and hosted providers such as Supabase and Neon ship their own.
servers.auth: A database user, or the provider's OAuth.
servers.notes: Check that the project you pick is still maintained.

servers.name: Stripe MCP server
servers.covers: Payments data and actions in Stripe.
servers.auth: OAuth or an agent API key.
servers.notes: Requires human confirmation before some writes such as refunds. Key requirements were changing, so check the current rules.

servers.name: Rovo MCP server
servers.covers: Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management and other Atlassian cloud products.
servers.notes: Cloud only. It does not help with self-hosted Jira.

servers.name: Stacksync MCP server
servers.covers: Lets an AI assistant build and run two-way syncs, workflows and Genies across the apps and databases connected to a Stacksync workspace, with the permissions of the person who signed in.
servers.auth: OAuth with your Stacksync login. No API key in the chat.
servers.notes: Works across many connected apps, not one. Read-only sign-in and approval before every change are available. Server URL: https://mcp.stacksync.com/mcp
